entries.maintainer: Paperclip Labs, Inc. (project publicly associated with pseudonymous developer @dotta)
entries.architecture: Node.js server + React UI + embedded/external PostgreSQL. 12 subsystems: Identity & Access, Org Chart & Agents, Work & Task System, Heartbeat Execution, Workspaces & Runtime, Governance & Approvals, Budget & Cost Control, Routines & Schedules, Plugins, Secrets & Storage, Activity & Events, Company Portability.
deployment_methods: local dev via pnpm + embedded Postgres
entries.api_mcp_interfaces: HTTP/REST API (default port 3100); MCP Tool Gateway & Apps for governed tool access; webhook triggers for routines
entries.authentication_model: trusted local loopback mode (default) or authenticated/private mode with LAN or Tailnet binding; per-agent API keys; short-lived run JWTs; board user accounts
entries.data_storage: PostgreSQL (local embedded or external); encrypted local secret storage; provider-backed object storage for attachments/work products
entries.networking_requirements: API server default port 3100; mobile dev server port 3101; optional Tailscale binding
entries.agent_job_model: Heartbeat-based execution on schedules and event triggers; agents have roles/titles/reporting lines/permissions/budgets; supports Claude Code, Codex, CLI agents, HTTP/webhook bots, external adapters
entries.webhooks_events: Routine system supports cron, webhook, and API triggers; durable activity log for mutating actions, heartbeat state, cost events, approvals, comments
entries.hermes_governance_overlap: Direct conceptual overlap with Hermes agent roles, scheduling/routines, worker heartbeats, budgets/cost control, and approvals. This is exactly the overlap the existing docs/beta/post-phase9/PAPERCLIP_ADAPTER.md and PAPERCLIP_CONTRACT.md already anticipate and constrain: Paperclip may project organizational/assignment state but Hermes remains sole admission, budget, and approval authority.
entries.security_supply_chain_notes: Checksum-verified install script; optional OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation; anonymous opt-in telemetry (disable via env/config); per-agent secret scoping; full audit log. No independent third-party security audit identified during this discovery pass.
entries.notes: Semantic fit with the pre-existing Hermes Paperclip adapter design (organizations, employees, projects, issues, assignments, comments, heartbeats, sessions, transcripts, skills, worktrees, checkpoints, cost/usage) is very high, which is corroborating but not conclusive evidence of intent. Operator confirmation of intended project identity is still recommended before any live wiring (Stage 2+).

entries.display_name: Buzz (Block, Inc.) — covers "Buzz Web" and "Buzz Relay"
entries.latest_stable_release: Not pinned to a numbered tag as of retrieval; repository is under active post-launch development (launched 2026-07-21).
entries.architecture: Single Rust (Axum) relay binary serves the WebSocket relay, REST API, and bundled web UI from one process. Desktop client is Tauri + React. buzz-cli provides a JSON-in/JSON-out interface for LLM tool calls. buzz-acp bridges external agent runtimes (Goose, Codex, Claude Code) to the relay.
deployment_methods: local dev: Docker Compose + Hermit toolchain
self-hosted VPS: production Compose bundle in deploy/compose/
entries.api_mcp_interfaces: WebSocket (primary), REST (secondary), Nostr NIP-01/NIP-42 (signed events, Schnorr auth), NIP-34 (git events), Blossom protocol (media)
entries.authentication_model: Nostr keypair identity for every participant (human or agent); Schnorr signatures; rate limiting via buzz-auth; no username/password model
entries.data_storage: PostgreSQL (events, audit log, full-text search); Redis (pub/sub, presence, typing — ephemeral); S3/MinIO via Blossom (media)
entries.networking_requirements: WebSocket + REST default port 3000 (ws://localhost:3000 in local dev); optional Caddy reverse proxy with TLS for production
entries.agent_job_model: Agents are scoped by cryptographic identity ("the same way you'd scope a teammate"), not permission flags; agents can read/post/react, create channels, run workflows and git operations, and execute shell commands via the buzz-cli tool interface
entries.webhooks_events: All activity (messages, reactions, workflow steps, review approvals, git events) is a signed Nostr event in one audit log; workflow triggers support message/reaction/schedule/webhook
entries.hermes_governance_overlap: Very high — buzz-cli's shell-execution and workflow-run capability, and buzz-acp's external-agent bridging, directly overlap Hermes's own admission/execution authority. This is exactly why docs/beta/post-phase9/BUZZ_RELAY_ADAPTER.md and BUZZ_SECURITY.md model Buzz strictly as a signed-event transport with zero independent execution, approval, or credential authority.
entries.security_supply_chain_notes: Apache-2.0, corporate-backed (Block/Square lineage), single relay binary reduces supply-chain surface versus a multi-service stack, but buzz-cli's direct shell-execution capability for agents is a meaningful risk that Hermes governance must intermediate, never expose directly.
entries.notes: "Buzz Web" is not a separate repository — the web UI is served by the same relay binary as "Buzz Relay". Treat Buzz Web and Buzz Relay as one upstream (github.com/block/buzz), not two.

No distinct upstream project named "Buzznode" was found. The closest concept in the verified Buzz upstream is buzz-acp (the agent/worker connection bridge inside github.com/block/buzz), which is a component of the single Buzz repository, not a standalone worker-host product. The existing internal design (docs/beta/post-phase9/BUZZNODE_ADAPTER.md) models Buzznode as a Hermes-side concept: a persistent, isolated worker-host capability that would connect to Buzz via buzz-acp. Recommendation: treat "Buzznode" as an internal Hermes worker-host classification that consumes the Buzz upstream, not as a separate external project to source. Operator should confirm this reading before Stage 6 live work begins.
evidence_source: WebSearch queries for "Buzznode", "Buzz Relay" combined with block/buzz README review, 2026-08-05

entries.notes: "Centralized Buzz agents/workers" maps to the existing Hermes-side worker/job contract (docs/beta/post-phase9/WORKER_JOB_CONTRACT.md, apps/sigil/src/sigil/buzz_relay_adapter.py, buzznode_adapter.py) that would consume Buzz's buzz-acp/buzz-cli interfaces under Hermes admission. entries.display_name: Alexa Smart Home Skills API / Custom Skills Kit (classic, self-serve)
entries.notes: Fully self-serve, publicly documented, requires AWS Lambda or HTTPS endpoint, OAuth2 account linking, and Amazon certification before publication. Models device control (lights, thermostats, locks, etc.), not general task delegation. This is the closest fully-open, non-partner-gated Alexa integration route available today.

Amazon's newest integration path (announced July 2026): brands bring their own MCP server, Alexa+ inspects it and generates a simulator-ready add-on package. Account linking uses OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code Grant with mandatory PKCE S256 (implicit grant not supported). As of retrieval, Alexa+ for Builders is stated to be "available to select partners working directly with Amazon's team" — not a general self-serve program. Classified as a plausible-but-unverified candidate for Hermes because (a) it is the only Alexa surface that matches Hermes's own MCP interfaces, but (b) general public availability, exact certification requirements, and whether a private/non-public MCP endpoint is acceptable to Amazon are unconfirmed.
